messages:
maria_support: Heads-up — multiple customers reporting a spike in 5xx (502/504) and timeouts to the hosted inference API since ~09:40 UTC. Getting escalation tickets with request IDs. Some customers see a steady stream of `gateway timeout` while others get `backend error`.

sam_sre: @maria_support can you paste a couple of request IDs and example timestamps? Also which endpoints are affected (generate/chat/embed)?

maria_support: Example request IDs — r-6f2a9c, r-6f2aab, r-6f2b0f. All from the text generation endpoint (v1/generate). Occurred for customers on us-west-2 and eu-west-1. First reports at 09:39 UTC. Ticket excerpts attached in Zendesk.

josh_prodeng: Observed an uptick in 5xx rate and 95/99th latency in our console dashboards starting at 09:38. Traces show upstream errors touching cache lookup layer (prefix KV). Many traces have error "KV_FETCH_ERROR: connection reset by peer" followed by subsequent 502.

leo_infra: Noted that our Redis cluster (prefix-cache-prod) had a rolling failover around 09:35 due to a node OOM. Replica promoted, but we probably had a cache stampede after nodes restarted. Metrics: evictions spiked, keyspace hits dropped to 2% for ~3m.

redis-oncall-bot: Alert: redis prefix-cache-prod: node-3 OOM -> SIGKILL at 09:34:12 UTC. Failover completed at 09:36:01 UTC. Current status: degraded, 1/6 nodes recovering. Alerts: high eviction ratio, slow commands.

sam_sre: This matches the traces. If prefix cache starts returning connection errors or slow replies, the runtime might be blocking waiting for KV lookups, causing request handlers to time out -> 504/gateway timeout. We should confirm whether the runtime has a circuit breaker and fallback path.

josh_prodeng: There is a fallback: if cache is unavailable we should bypass and fetch directly from model state (but that code path hasn't been exercised in a while). Logs show we didn't hit bypass — instead got exceptions from the cache client that propagate as 502. Looks like the client is raising instead of returning a transient miss.

katie_cs: A customer just messaged that their app sees ~5% success, rest 502s. They're on dedicated dedicated-xyz but using hosted cache service for prefix caching. They want ETA.

maria_support: Action: escalating to infra SRE + runtime. Sam/Josh please coordinate. I'll update customers with "investigating" and share request IDs.

sam_sre: Immediate mitigation steps I'm putting in motion:
1) Enable runtime cache-bypass feature flag for affected regions so requests skip remote prefix cache and use local in-process cache/fallback. This will raise token costs but restore availability.
2) Increase Redis client timeout to avoid tight exception bubbling (temp change).
3) If needed, add short-term rate limit on cache-heavy endpoints to reduce stampede.

leo_infra: I'm on node recovery. Plan: disable RDB/AOF temporarily on affected cluster to prevent extra I/O, and widen maxmemory-policy to noeviction for a minute while we stabilize (will risk rejecting writes though). Also provisioning an extra replica to absorb traffic.

josh_prodeng: How do we flip the runtime flag? Is there a console toggle or service push? We need low-friction path.

sam_sre: Console toggle exists: feature.flag.cache_prefix.bypass -> set to true for env=prod, region=us-west-2,eu-west-1. I'll flip now.

sam_sre: Flipped the flag at 09:46 UTC for the two regions.

maria_support: Sent update to affected customers: "We've detected an issue with our prefix caching dependency causing intermittent 5xx/timeouts; we're enabling a bypass and working on the cache cluster. ETA unknown; will update in 15m." :eyes:

redis-oncall-bot: Change: feature.flag.cache_prefix.bypass=true applied to prod us-west-2,eu-west-1 at 09:46:12 UTC by sam_sre.

leo_infra: Node recovery: disabled RDB snapshots and increased maxmemory from 180GB -> 220GB on node-3. Replica added (node-7) at 09:50. Evictions falling but still high.

josh_prodeng: After bypass flip, we see success rates rise to ~92% and 5xx rate drop — latency still a bit elevated because runtime does more work without cached prefixes but overall availability recovering.

sam_sre: Posting quick repro steps for debugging (useful for root cause and postmortem):

1) Simulate cache storm: use redis-benchmark or our load harness to perform lots of GET/SET on prefix keys with TTL churn. e.g.: 

```
redis-benchmark -h <host> -p <port> -c 100 -n 100000 -t get,set --csv
```

2) Capture client errors from runtime (logs):
```
2026-02-12T09:34:55Z ERROR runtime.cache_prefix: KV_FETCH_ERROR request_id=r-6f2a9c err="read: connection reset by peer"
```

3) Check Redis INFO stats: keyspace_hits, rejected_clients, rejected_connections, used_memory, mem_fragmentation_ratio, evicted_keys

4) Reproduce via our internal harness hitting v1/generate with identical prompt sequences that cause heavy prefix reuse.

josh_prodeng: Root causes hypotheses:
- Memory pressure caused node OOM -> SIGKILL -> failover causing cache cold start and stampede
- Client library has aggressive behavior on connection errors (throws) instead of returning transient miss, which bubbles up as 5xx
- No circuit breaker on KV layer for p95 requests causing runtime threads to block

sam_sre: Immediate post-incident remediation tasks (assigning):
- leo_infra: complete cluster stabilization and ensure no further OOMs (check config, add swap?); increase alerts for mem usage before OOM
- josh_prodeng: implement circuit breaker + soft-fail path if KV client is erroring (runtime should treat as cache miss, not fatal)
- infra: review Redis maxclients and connection pool sizing on runtime side
- prodeng: add a throttling policy so we don't pump huge synchronous lookup storms during failover

katie_cs: Customers appreciate the quick mitigation. Please add a short summary for support to paste into tickets once incident is declared over.

maria_support: Will prepare a templated update once we have root cause and ETA for permanent fix.

leo_infra: Note for postmortem: check if RDB snapshotting or eviction policy contributed. Also confirm whether our autoscaler tried to reschedule pods during the failover window which may have added load.

sam_sre: Current status at 09:55 UTC: bypass still enabled, availability ~95%, redis cluster degraded but recovering. Keeping incident open. Next update in 20 minutes or when major change.

maria_support: Adding to ticket: "mitigation: cache-bypass enabled; infra recovering Redis cluster; root cause under investigation (eviction/oom)."

josh_prodeng: Quick code snippet to defensively handle KV client errors (to be PR'd):
```
try {
  val = kvClient.get(key)
} catch (TransientConnectionException e) {
  // treat as cache miss, record metric kv.error_as_miss
  val = null
}
```

sam_sre: Also adding metric and alert: if kv.errors_as_5xx > 0.5% of requests for 5m, auto-enable bypass and page infra.

redis-oncall-bot: Note: scheduled maintenance window canceled for prefix-cache-prod today due to recovery. All future maintenance to be coordinated with SRE.

maria_support: Thanks everyone. I'll keep customers informed. Please paste any final notes here and I'll fold them into support communications.

sam_sre: Final quick note: we should add a playbook step to flip bypass and notify customers automatically during prefix-cache outages. Filing follow-up ticket INFRA-4821.

josh_prodeng: Filing runtime follow-up to add circuit breaker: RUNTIME-1307. Adding tests for cache failure scenarios.

leo_infra: Marking redis cluster stable at 10:12 UTC but will monitor for 2h. Closing action on immediate node OOM cause (investigating root cause of OOM later). :white_check_mark:

maria_support: Incident note for support: "09:34 UTC - Redis prefix-cache cluster experienced OOM -> failover -> eviction storm -> runtime cache client errors -> uptick in 5xx and timeouts. Mitigation: enabled cache-bypass and recovered cluster. Ongoing follow-ups: circuit breaker, connection pool tuning, alert tuning."
